text:
[IMAGE_DIAGRAM | Page 41] Box 4. Climate-induced migration in Vietnam
Text box discussing climate-induced migration in Vietnam. It notes that climate change could significantly increase internal migration, especially to urban areas, with 25-33 percent of all internal migrants in Vietnam by 2050 estimated to be climate migrants depending on climate and socioeconomic development trajectories. Hanoi and the Red River Delta are projected to be the largest hotspots for climate in-migration by 2050, alongside smaller hotspots in the coastal central region (Bin Dinh, Quang Ngai, and Quang Tri provinces). Conversely, the Mekong Delta and areas around HCMC are projected to be the largest climate out-migration hotspots by 2050 due to sea-level rise and storm surges. Source: Clement et al., 2021.

metadata.title: Box 4. Climate-induced migration in Vietnam

text:
[TABLE | Page 50] Box 6. Ten technical highlights of the Accelerated Decarbonization Scenario
Ten technical highlights of the Accelerated Decarbonization Scenario listed as bullet points (i to x): i. Installed capacity of coal power plants peaks in 2025 and coal usage is phased out with small footprint remaining by 2040; ii. Power sector-related emissions peak in 2030 and are below 2020 levels by 2040; iii. Share of fossil fuels is less than 10 percent of generation capacity in 2040; iv. Renewable energy technologies (solar, on-shore, off-shore wind) dominate the power system accounting for up to 90 percent of installed capacity; v. Importance of overcoming intermittency and reliability created by large-scale renewable deployment for base load power and managing peak load; vi. Significant capacity of energy storage systems (batteries, pumped hydropower) needed; vii. Capacity and flexibility of the power grid need to be significantly increased; viii. Power system modeling should be carried out periodically to update investment decisions; ix. Natural gas plays a role as a transition fuel until other clean technologies become more cost-efficient; x. Unbalanced implementation or timing mismatch of required clean energy investments could create energy security concerns and a risk of retreating to coal.

metadata.title: Box 6. Ten technical highlights of the Accelerated Decarbonization Scenario

[IMAGE_DIAGRAM | Page 61] Box 8. Vietnam’ shift toward environmental goods exports and emerging opportunities
The box describes Vietnam's shift toward environmental goods exports and emerging opportunities. Key facts: Vietnam's trade in environmental products mostly involves renewable energy. Solar cells and heliostats exports showed exceptional annual growth rates from 2010 to 2020 of 81.6 percent and 71.2 percent, respectively. The solar photovoltaic (PV) cell sector is a niche often embedded in complex value chains. Vietnam is a major player in solar equipment but can position itself in wind-related technologies and electrical equipment, though policies enacted by trading partners may affect trade, suggesting market diversification (e.g., African Continental Free Trade Area).
